proof_attempt_summary: Discovery built a residual-Hermite estimator, an anisotropic quadrature construction, and uniform-design hard instances, then enlarged the covariate class and repaired the converse proofs by subclass inclusion. The D0.5 audit left the Gauss–Hermite moments leaf without a sufficient proof or citation, making the anisotropic chi-square bound and matched-frontier converses conditional; it graded the delivered package incremental, below the field floor. This archive records the attempted proof and unresolved finding, not an established sound matched-frontier theorem.
tldr: For iid data with an arbitrary Borel covariate law on \([0,1]\), a known Gaussian--Rademacher treatment channel is statistically almost Gaussian when \(na^8\) is small, yet its compact component permits nuisance-robust causal-slope recovery beyond ordinary covariance. Over the exact class with arbitrary measurable bounded nuisances, a total growing-degree residual-Hermite estimator attains squared risk \(r_{n,a}=n^{-1}+h^2\{\log\log(e^e+nh^2)/\log(e+nh^2)\}^2\). The revalidated positive compact two-slope construction gives the uniform anisotropic chi-square bound \(Ch^2(C'/k)^{2k}\); after restricting the hard experiment to the uniform-design subfamily contained in the arbitrary-design class, it yields the matching all-estimator converse and the \(90\%\)-honest connected-interval expected-length order \(\sqrt{r_{n,a}}\).
gap: Existing partially linear theory either imposes nuisance-learning rates, treats exact Gaussian noise, assumes a fixed nonzero cumulant, or bounds a restricted exact-null score family. Generic compact Gaussian-mixture moduli do not retain the shrinking treatment-coordinate factor needed for this causal experiment.
fill: The project supplies a total observable estimator, an all-estimator same-class lower bound, and a matched honest connected-interval frontier. Its decisive new analytic object is an anisotropic positive-mixture chi-square modulus with an explicit \(h^2\) gain.
